author: Brenton Kemp
title: Spencer Horwitz to be placed on 10-day IL Thursday
desc: The Pirates will place first baseman Spencer Horwitz (hamstring) on the 10-day injured list on Thursday.
impact: Horwitz suffered a hamstring injury in Wednesday's blowout of the Mariners and will need some time to heal. The 28-year-old has enjoyed a strong season, hitting .288 with 10 homers and an .841 OPS across 74 games this season. Jack Brannigan has been summoned from the minors in a corresponding move.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Jack Brannigan to join Pirates Thursday
desc: Pirates infielder Jack Brannigan has joined the Pirates for Thursday's contest against the Mariners.
impact: Brannigan joins the Pirates on Thursday morning to take the roster spot of infielder Spencer Horwitz, who will be placed on the 10-day injured list with a hamstring injury. The 25-year-old has yet to make his MLB debut and has hit .231 with 11 homers and an .864 OPS in 42 games between High-A and Double-A this season.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Justin Verlander (hamstring) resumes playing catch
desc: Tigers right-hander Justin Verlander (hamstring) has resumed playing catch.
impact: Verlander was set to return to the Tigers' rotation from hip inflammation on Sunday, but suffered a left hamstring strain during a June 17 side session. He has made just one start for the team this season and is expected to miss multiple weeks before a potential return.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Jordan Westburg (elbow) begins running progression
desc: Orioles infielder Jordan Westburg (elbow) has begun a running progression and should be ready for the start of Spring Training in 2027.
impact: Westburg underwent Tommy John surgery on May 13 and will miss the remainder of the 2026 season. He said he will be ready to begin spring training on time in 2027 as his running progression marks the first notable step in his rehab progress.

author: Nate Miller
title: Derek Hill delivers in the clutch
desc: Derek Hill hit a two-run homer in his only at-bat during Wednesday's 5-4 win over the Nationals.
impact: With the Phillies down by one with one on and two outs, manager Don Mattingly called on the recently acquired Hill to pinch hit for rookie Justin Crawford. That decision proved to be a wise one, as Hill ripped a two-run shot that ended up being the game winner. It was Hill's first home run for the Phillies, and the 30-year-old outfielder is now 7-for-21 with three RBI in a Philly uniform.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Michael Grove recalled from Triple-A
desc: The Rays have recalled right-hander Michael Grove from Triple-A Durham.
impact: Grove was recently activated from the 60-day injured list and sent to Durham after recovering from March 2025 surgery to repair a torn labrum in his right shoulder. He last posted a 5.12 ERA across 39 outings (two starts) in 2024 while with the Dodgers.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Steven Matz (ankle) placed on 15-day IL
desc: The Rays have placed left-hander Steven Matz on the 15-day injured list with a left ankle sprain.
impact: Matz's last five outings have come out of the Rays' bullpen, but he was shelled for five earned runs in two innings against the Royals on Monday before being placed on the IL on Wednesday. The veteran has limped to a 6.28 ERA across 15 outings (10 starts) this season. Right-hander Michael Grove was recalled from Triple-A Durham in a corresponding move.

author: Nate Miller
title: Jhoan Duran picks up first save in two weeks
desc: Jhoan Duran struck out the side in order during a spotless bottom of the ninth inning to earn the save in Wednesday's 5-4 win over the Nationals.
impact: Duran is up to 19 saves on the season, but this was his first chance in two full weeks. The flame-throwing righty now sports a 1.69 ERA with an outstanding 43-5 K/BB ratio across 26 2/3 innings on the season. He's among the elite closers in the league.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Nathan Lukes homers in loss to Astros Wednesday
desc: Blue Jays outfielder Nathan Lukes went 1-for-3 with a solo home run in a 3-1 loss to the Astros on Wednesday.
impact: Lukes slugged a solo homer in the bottom of the first in retaliation against an Astros first-inning run of their own. Unfortunately, the Blue Jays would go scoreless for the next eight innings while the Astros scored a couple of runs late to win this one by a 3-1 score. The long ball was Lukes' third of the season, and while he's not known specifically for his power, he's still slashing .301/.344/.420 for the season, a line that puts his wRC+ at 114, 14 percent above the league average.

author: Nate Miller
title: Aaron Nola turns in another respectable effort Wednesday night
desc: Aaron Nola allowed two runs on three hits and two walks while striking out five over five innings in Wednesday's 5-4 win over the Nationals.
impact: The long ball continues to plague Nola, as he allowed solo shots in the first and second innings of Wednesday's game. However, that was all the scoring the Nationals mustered against the veteran righty, as Nola settled down and rolled off three straight shutout frames before leaving after the fifth. His ERA still sits at an ugly 5.58 with a 1.45 WHIP through 16 starts, but Nola is showing positive signs going into the second half of the season. He'll face the Pirates on Monday.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Daulton Varsho collects two hits, stolen base in loss to Astros
desc: Blue Jays outfielder Daulton Varsho went 2-for-4 with a stolen base in a 3-1 loss to the Astros on Wednesday.
impact: A day after going 3-for-6 with a homer and a pair of doubles, Varsho recorded another multi-hit effort on Wednesday. Unfortunately, his two hits accounted for half of his team's total in a quiet night at the plate for the Blue Jays. Varsho has been a streaky hitter in the past, but does boast a solid comination of power and speed as his stolen base on Wednesday was his seventh of the season to go along with seven homers in 255 plate appearances. He is a solid waiver wire look while he is swinging the bat the way he is, in addition to his speed.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Trey Yesavage walks five in no-decision against Astros Wednesday
desc: Blue Jays right-hander Trey Yesavage allowed one earned run on two hits and five walks across 5 2/3 innings in a no-decision against the Astros on Wednesday.
impact: Yesavage did a fine job of limiting hits and runs on the evening, but he handed out five free passes while striking out five on the evening. While he fell just one out shy of a quality start, the outing feels ominous as this one was the third time in his last six starts in which he has walked at least five after walking six on June 12 against the Yankees and seven on May 30 against the Orioles. He sports a solid 3.56 ERA through 11 starts, but also a 4.65 xFIP and a 4.58 SIERA as his middling 58:30 K:BB in 60 2/3 innings leaves something to be desired.

author: Nate Miller
title: Joey Bart smacks two-run homer Wednesday night
desc: Joey Bart went 2-for-4 with a two-run homer in Wednesday's 5-2 loss to the Padres.
impact: Bart provided all of the run production for the suddenly struggling Braves on Wednesday. The 29-year-old backstop hit his first homer since joining the Braves in the sixth inning, helping the club get back in the ball game, at least briefly. Bart has now gone 2-for-11 with three RBI since being traded to Atlanta, and he should remain in a backup role to starter Drake Baldwin going forward.

author: Brenton Kemp
title: Rhett Lowder hit with loss Wednesday versus Brewers
desc: Reds right-hander Rhett Lowder surrendered three earned runs on eight hits across 5 2/3 innings on Wednesday, taking the loss at home against the Brewers.
impact: Two of the eight hits Lowder yielded on the night went for home runs, while he also walked one and struck out six. He also didn't receive much offensive support while in the contest as the Reds were down 3-1 upon his departure in an eventual 6-5 loss. Since starting the season 3-1, Lowder has lost his last four decisions and hasn't reached six innings completed since April 20, a span of seven starts. He will bring a 4.81 ERA into his next scheduled outing, which is lined up for early next week in a rematch against the Brewers in Milwaukee.

author: Bruno Mulé
title: Bo Bichette stays hot with 10th homer
desc: Bo Bichette went 2-for-4 with a solo home run and a double in the Mets' 10-5 loss to the Cubs in the second game of Wednesday's doubleheader. He took Gavin Hollowell deep in the sixth inning before adding a double in the eighth.
impact: Bichette has hit five of his 10 home runs over his last 13 games while batting .388 during that stretch. His recent surge has helped offset a slow start to the season.
